title: stratified-span-sampling-and-sharded-cost-histograms-for-heavy-tail-requests
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces stratified span sampling with priority-based retention and per-model-shard token-cost histograms. Adds console dashboard panels and alert tuning knobs for long-tail request cost spikes.
description:
Motivation: Observability spend and storage growth have been driven by a small fraction of high-latency/long-token sessions. This PR introduces two complementary features to reduce O(1) trace storage costs while preserving signal for the heavy tail: 1) Stratified span sampling: deterministic, priority-aware sampling that keeps a bounded number of representative long spans per route and per time window; 2) Sharded cost histograms: per-model_shard token-cost and latency histograms to make unit economics visible across shards and to enable targeted tuning.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- Runtime: add a sampling controller that applies stratified reservoir sampling for spans. Sampling keys: (route_id, model_shard, latency_bucket). Retention priority influenced by span.duration, token_count, and error_flag. Configurable via feature flag and route-level overrides.
- Tracing: add new span tag `sample_priority` and `shard_hist_key`; emit sampled span-rate metadata to the tracing backend.
- Metrics: export sharded histograms for token-cost and per-token latency (HISTOGRAM_BUCKETS tuned to heavy-tail). Add derived metrics: shard_p50/p90/p99_token_cost and shard_token_cost_rate.
- Console/Dashboards: new "Sharded Cost" dashboard with small-multiples by model_shard and a long-tail resource usage panel. New alert rules that trigger on sustained shard_token_cost_rate increases (with dynamic baselining).
- Config: add `observability.sampling.stratified` config block and route-level annotations to opt in/out or set custom retention budgets.
- Tests: unit tests for sampling controller, e2e for metric emission, snapshot tests for dashboard JSON.

Rollout & migration notes: 
- This PR is feature-flag gated (observability.stratified_sampling.enabled=false by default). Admins can enable per-tenant or global.
- Backwards compatibility: sampled spans include a `legacy_sampled` flag while rolling out; metric keys use stable naming to avoid aliasing.
- Storage: default retention budget limits retained spans per (route, shard, hour) to 500 to prevent unbounded growth. Operators can increase budgets for debug modes.

Performance and cost impact: 
- In canary (alpha) we observed ~68% reduction in span writes from the heavy-tail cohort while retaining >92% of unique error signatures. Exported metric cardinality increased slightly due to per-shard histograms (+~6%), but overall storage cost decreased due to sampling.

Alerting changes: 
- Added `SLO-Observability-HighShardCost` which triggers when a shard_token_cost_rate rises >2x baseline for >10m. Baseline uses 90-day rolling median by default and can be tuned per-tenant.
- Reduced noisy pager churn by using a two-stage alert: brief warning (no page) then critical if sustained.

Notes for on-call and SRE: 
- If you see large gaps in traces for a route after enabling, check `observability.sampling.debug` route annotation; temporarily set to `retain_all` to capture a full traffic window.
- Use `console/dashboards/sharded_cost` to identify which model_shard is contributing to token-cost anomalies.

Overall this PR aims to reduce long-tail observability cost while preserving signal needed to debug latency and cost regressions per shard.
notes: Canaryed on alpha cluster for 72h, storage down ~34%, heavy-tail span writes down ~68%. Operators should review `platform/config/schema.yaml` before enabling globally.
